holidays.name: National Scotch Day
holidays.description: A day for sipping Scotch whisky, whether neat, on the rocks, or with a splash of water. Fans of smoky peat and oak-aged goodness raise a dram in honor of Scotland's most famous liquid export.
holidays.origin: An unofficial food and drink observance, likely popularized by spirits enthusiasts and social media. Scotch whisky itself has been recorded in Scotland since at least 1494, when the Exchequer Rolls mention malt used to make aqua vitae.
holidays.funFact: By law, Scotch whisky must be aged in oak barrels in Scotland for at least three years, and there are more barrels of maturing whisky in Scotland than people living there.

holidays.name: National Crème Brûlée Day
holidays.description: A celebration of the creamy custard dessert with a crackly caramelized sugar top. The best part is the satisfying tap of a spoon breaking through the glassy crust.
holidays.origin: An unofficial food holiday created by dessert lovers. The dish is claimed by France, England (as Trinity Cream at Cambridge), and Spain (as Crema Catalana), and all three love to argue about who made it first.
holidays.funFact: Many restaurants caramelize the sugar with a small kitchen blowtorch, which makes crème brûlée one of the few desserts where setting it on fire is considered good technique.

holidays.name: Take Your Pants for a Walk Day
holidays.description: A cheerfully absurd observance encouraging people to take their pants out for some fresh air. Interpretations vary from wearing them proudly in public to literally leashing them and strolling around the block.
holidays.origin: This is a humorous, unofficial holiday that spread through quirky holiday calendars and social media. Nobody seems to know who first thought pants were in need of exercise.
holidays.funFact: The word 'pants' is short for 'pantaloons,' a style of trousers named after Pantalone, a stock character in Italian commedia dell'arte theater.

holidays.name: National Walk on Stilts Day
holidays.description: A day for lifting yourself a few feet off the ground and seeing the world from a taller perspective. Celebrants are encouraged to strap on stilts and stride around with the confidence of a very wobbly giraffe.
holidays.origin: An unofficial quirky holiday celebrating one of the oldest forms of performance and practical transport. Stilts have been used for centuries by shepherds in marshy areas like Les Landes in France to cross wet terrain and watch their flocks.
holidays.funFact: In the Landes region of France, shepherds on stilts, called tchanquès, were a common sight until the 19th century, and some could reportedly walk faster on stilts than most people could on foot.

holidays.name: Korean War Veterans Armistice Day
holidays.description: A solemn U.S. observance honoring the veterans of the Korean War on the anniversary of the 1953 armistice that halted the fighting. It is a day for remembering service and sacrifice during a conflict often called 'The Forgotten War.'
holidays.origin: The armistice agreement was signed on July 27, 1953, ending active combat in Korea. The U.S. observance has been recognized by presidential proclamation as National Korean War Veterans Armistice Day.
holidays.funFact: Technically, no peace treaty was ever signed to end the Korean War, so the two Koreas remain officially in a state of war under the armistice.
